pageCache.pageTitle: St Piran's Independent Primary School - Headmaster's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headmaster's Welcome
I am delighted to welcome you to St Piran's School, one of the most exciting, inspirational and family-centred preparatory schools in the country.
Our much-loved school might have 200 years of history behind it, but it is always looking to the future. We continue to push the boundaries of academic excellence, artistic flair, sporting prowess and personal development within our clear Christian ethos.
I feel blessed to have joined this very special community. From the moment I walked through the doors, I knew this was the school for us.
My children, like yours, will experience a truly personal journey where they will feel valued and able to flourish, supported by inspiring teachers and an array of superb educational, extracurricular and sporting facilities. Happy children succeed, and we place the relationships between staff, children and parents at the forefront of all we do.
As a Headmaster, I believe that a key role is to serve my staff so that they deliver an exceptional education for each child. I want my teachers to impart a passion for each area of the curriculum, engulf children in positivity and communicate the potential of every child so clearly that they are inspired to see it in themselves. We truly believe that the most beautiful thing a child can wear is confidence.
From the moment your child walks through our doors to that final Leavers' Ceremony, they will be treated and nurtured as individuals.
We embed our Learning Habits into all aspects of school life; they are:
We use our head to THINK
We use our hands to ENGAGE
We use our heart to be MOTIVATED
Through these Learning Habits, we bring passion and fun to learning, creating curiosity and a desire to learn more. This is why I truly believe that St Piran’s inspires confidence in all our pupils and equips them with the right foundation to succeed in all that they go on to do.
The world of St Piran's awaits, and it would be my privilege to show you its wonders.
Sebastian Sales Headmaster

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Our Early Years Department
Our Early Years Department is closely aligned with the whole school approach and is linked to the Characteristics of Effective Learning in Early Years. At the heart of our teaching philosophy are our Leadership Habits - Motivation, Engagement and Thinking, which guide both how we teach and how children learn. We believe that knowing how a child learns is just as important as what they learn, and we strive to achieve this through everything we do.
Our Early Years provision is made up of three carefully structured phases, each designed to meet the developmental needs of children at every stage of their early learning journey:
A warm, home-from-home environment led by an experienced team of qualified Early Years professionals. With high staff-to-child ratios, our Nursery focuses on the three Prime Areas of learning: Communication and Language, Personal, Social and Emotional Development, and Physical Development. Children have the opportunity to eat, sleep, play, and toilet train all under one roof, giving them a consistent and nurturing routine to build a strong foundation for future learning.
Building on everything offered in our Nursery, our Pre-School provides a more structured approach to early learning whilst maintaining a strong focus on learning through play. Children are introduced to our Read Write Inc. (RWI) phonics scheme, supporting early reading skills and preparing them for their transition into Reception.
There is a stronger emphasis on number sense, helping children to develop an early understanding of number and laying the groundwork for future mathematical learning.
Finger gym activities and a focus on gross motor development support muscle strength and control, providing the essential foundations for future handwriting and fine motor skills. Children also continue to grow in independence, confidence, and social awareness through carefully planned experiences and routines.
Reception continues to build on all that has been established in Pre-School, with a strong emphasis on growing independence and encouraging children to take more responsibility for their learning and routines.
The Early Years curriculum remains at the heart of our approach, with a progressive focus on literacy, writing, and mathematics, ensuring children are well-prepared for Key Stage 1. Children enjoy IT and French lessons, designed specifically for their age group to make learning fun, interactive, and engaging.
Learning remains play-based, supporting development through children’s own interests and curiosity. Small class sizes and a well-staffed team allow for tailored support, helping every child make strong progress from their individual starting points.
From the very beginning in Nursery right through to the end of Reception, each child benefits from an individualised learning plan, ensuring that their needs, interests, and potential are fully understood and nurtured throughout their time in Early Years.
What our Early Years department offers
Our Early Years team offers a nurturing, play-based environment focused on how children learn as much as what they learn. Aligned with our school’s Leadership Habits of Motivation, Engagement, and Thinking, we support every child’s unique journey from Nursery (2–3 years) through Pre-School (3–4 years) and Reception (4–5 years).
We offer specialist lessons from 2 years old including swimming, football, music, woodland learning, yoga & mindfulness, plus wrap around care and Reception after-school clubs. Our tailored support helps children develop confidence, resilience, and a lifelong love of learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Stretch & Support Programme at St Piran's School Maidenhead
pageCache.text:
Stretch & Support
At St. Piran's, our teachers prioritise the development of each individual student and cater to their unique needs. We understand that children learn at different rates, some requiring further challenges while others need extra assistance. As a school, we utilise various methods to assess where each student is on their learning journey, and we have established structures to ensure that they exceed their own expectations. Our stretch program, Blaze, and our support program, Tutor Point, provide the necessary support and guidance for students to grasp new ideas and concepts, thus enabling them to have a deeper understanding of their subjects. Additionally, we equip them with strategies, tools, and techniques that they can utilise in the classroom and self-learning.
Blaze
All children in the school are offered stretch in each element of the curriculum. The Blaze programme offers challenges beyond the classroom, sports pitch or music suite. The programme challenges the more able to develop greater depth in terms of competitions, visits etc.
Tailored Learning Centre
At St. Piran's, our teachers prioritise the development of each individual student and cater to their unique needs. Within our TLC, we ensure that children are provided with both stretch and support provision, and given the tools to enable them to have a deeper understanding of their subjects. We understand that children learn at different rates, some requiring further challenges while others need extra assistance. As a school, we utilise various methods to assess where each student is on their learning journey, and we have established structures to ensure that they exceed their own expectations. Additionally, we equip them with strategies, tools, and techniques that they can utilise in the classroom and self-learning.
At St Piran’s we celebrate neurodiversity and recognise that everybody’s brain is wired in its own unique way. It is with this in mind, that we ensure our teaching in the classroom caters for a range of learning styles; visual learners, auditory learners and kinaesthetic learners. As you take a walk around the classrooms you will notice that children are supported through high quality teaching and reasonable classroom adjustments to ensure the environment is correct to enable the best learning to take place for each individual pupil.
Where our pupils require a little extra 1:1 support to enable them to master a skill or help them to catch up with their learning gaps, our specialist teachers can offer 1:1 lessons outside the classroom. These lessons are tailored specifically to the individuals needs and our tutors work with a range of professionals and link closely with school staff to ensure they create a bespoke multisensory individual support plan going forwards. Parents are able to meet with the tutor point teachers each term to review progress.
We also support small groups of children across the school with additional interventions that include; sensory circuits, Lego therapy, Zones of Regulation, LG and walks and talks with our school dog Willow.
As a department, we value the positive relationships we build with parents. This is done through individual meetings, termly tea and talks and an open-door policy. Tea and talk is an opportunity for the school and parental body to support each other and share valuable resources. Feedback received from parents about this is that it is a wonderfully supportive community offering valuable feedback.
Our higher skilled children are stretched and challenged within their lessons. They are given opportunities outside the classroom to showcase and develop their skills, enabling them to reach their full potential. We are committed to providing a challenging curriculum for all pupils so that they continue to make progress. Overall, our ambition is to provide high-performing, challenging and future-focused learning for all.
With the help of the TLC Department, all children are encouraged to cultivate a positive approach to learning and develop the confidence to participate fully in all that the school offers.

pageCache.pageTitle: The History of our Independent Primary School
pageCache.text:
School History
St Piran's can trace its origins to 1805 when pupils, including Benjamin Disraeli, the future Prime Minister, received their early education at a small school in Blackheath, called Eliot Place.
The school moved to its present site in 1872 while Thomas Nunns was the Headmaster, to gain from the better air and the space to play sports. Plenty of space was essential for the sons of the gentry and aspiring gentry! Cordwalles School was born and remained a successful boys' boarding school for the next 47 years.
In 1919, Major Vernon Seymour Bryant became Headmaster. He was born in Truro, Cornwall and after being educated in Exeter and then Downing College, Cambridge, he became an assistant master at Wellington. He bought Cordwalles School for £7,700 and in the Year Book of 1920 it read, "Cordwalles is no more! Long live St. Piran's!" as Major Bryant bestowed on his school the name of the Patron Saint of Cornwall. His philosophy: "Boys will have the opportunity of becoming good craftsmen in workshops, libraries and field. Young boys can be set to work with machinery, heavy machinery, such as will excite the imagination and create the scientific sense."
23 boys started in 1920 at St. Piran's and by 1921 there were 65 on the books paying 50 guineas each per term. In 1972 the school became an educational trust with a Board of Governors and about 180 boys. Many additions were made to the building in the seventies including an outdoor swimming pool, an assembly hall, a new gymnasium, a library and a science laboratory.
In 1993, the school became fully co-educational, accepting boys and girls from ages three to thirteen. Boarding came to an end at St. Piran's after 188 years and the school adapted to the demands of the local market, becoming a local school meeting local needs. Further developments under Andrew Blumer included the building of the St. Piran's Centre, providing outstanding swimming, dance and sports facilities for the pupils.
The school continued to grow under Jonathan Carroll's headship from 2001-2019 with, amongst other things, a new Reception building, the development of our all-weather pitch and the end of schooling to age 13.
St Piran's, now with Sebastian Sales at the helm, remains a highly successful and respected Independent Preparatory School. Pupil numbers are higher than ever, with over 400 children attending the school. We would hope that the Reverend John Potticary would approve of what his small school from Blackheath has become, two hundred years on.
St Piran - The School's Namesake
St Piran was born in Ireland. After studying the scriptures in Rome he returned and was made a Bishop. In Ireland, he was said to have performed many miracles, such as raising from the dead soldiers slain in battle. But the Kings of Ireland at the time were not impressed. It is reported that in the 5th Century, St Piran was flung into the sea in Ireland. He had a millstone around his neck, but miraculously he floated across the water to Perran Beach in Perranporth.
It was here that he built a small chapel. St Piran built his oratory amongst the sand dunes. People would come from miles around to hear him preach there.
St Piran discovered tin too, but quite by accident. A black stone on his fire leaked a white liquid. St Piran had discovered tin.
The Cornish Flag, the Flag Of St Piran (white cross on a black background) represents white tin flowing from the black rock, or good overcoming evil. St Piran is the Patron Saint of Tin Miners.
St Piran is believed to have lived for 200 years. He was fond of a drink and met his end falling down a well. No date of his death was recorded.
St Piran is one of three Patron Saints Of Cornwall. The other two are St Michael and St Petroc. Michael is associated with St Michael's Mount and St Petroc with Padstow.
Cornwall's St Michael has his own feast day celebrated on May 8th, and St Petroc has 4th June.
St Piran's Day is on March 5th each year and the main celebrations are in Perranporth. The school celebrates with the Millstone Race and everyone dresses in black and white. The Headteacher has a millstone in his office and the garden near the Lower Hall is named the Millstone.

pageCache.text:
Academic
We are blessed with a truly inspirational staff who know and care for their pupils and are passionate about their subjects. The aim of the curriculum is to provide pupils with a stimulating and broad education in a nurturing environment; preparing them at every step for the challenges that they will face in the next stage of their educational journey.
The curriculum is the building blocks from which gifted teachers craft the adventure of learning. All topics are approached using our learning habits M.E.T. (Motivation, Engagement and Thinking).
Learning Habits
Motivation is the HEART, creating passion and a love for a topic.
Engagement is the HAND, the doing and trial and error aspect of learning.
Thinking is the HEAD, the figuring something out and reading around a topic to fully understand something.
Although the learning habits are the core of what we do and form the nucleus of our learning philosophy we also build other life skills throughout their learning opportunities. These life skills are a tool kit for the pupils that will ensure as they move on from St Piran's they do so with the skills needed for a 21st Century citizen. These we call our Leadership Habits.
We are extremely proud of the academic progress our pupils make whilst they are with us. They go on to Senior schools and are awarded scholarships in many fields of study, not just academia.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Academic Philosophy at St Piran's School Maidenhead, Berkshire
pageCache.text:
Our Philosophy
Our educational philosophy revolves around the symbiotic relationship of head, heart, and hand. At our school, we embody this as Motivation, Engagement, and Thinking. When pupils are driven by passion (Heart) for a subject, their active involvement (Hand) increases, fostering deeper analytical thinking (Head).
Our Learning Habits
Motivation is the HEART, creating passion and a love for a topic.
Engagement is the HAND, the doing and trial and error aspect of learning.
When we think (HEAD), we engage our minds in a process of understanding and problem-solving. It involves analysing a topic and gathering information to achieve comprehension.
Our focus on Learning Habits is central to our approach and is consistently reinforced throughout the school. This instils a lifelong love of learning in our students. As they become more adept at utilising these habits, we introduce additional life skills and help them build a strong tool kit. By the time students reach Year 6 and assume leadership positions, they have a wealth of skills that have become second nature through consistent practice. We refer to this collection of skills as our Leadership Habits.
